messages:
maria_sales: Quick sync — ACME Corp wants committed throughput numbers for their SOW. They're asking for 200 qps peaky with 1.5k token avg responses, plus an allowance for spikes to 400 qps for 15m windows. Can we confirm how many reserved GPUs they'd need and what autoscale fallback looks like?
ethan_sre: short answer: depends on model variant + batch settings. longer: 1 G5-16-like GPU typically ~60-80 qps at 1.5k tokens if using non-quantized fp16 model; with 4:1 batching we might push more but latency suffers.
liyah_se: we should map to their latency SLOs. mary says they need p50 < 250ms for interactive endpoints, p95 < 1.2s. those constraints reduce batching headroom.
noah_sales_engineering: pricing side: customer expects committed discount on reserved capacity. need an estimate of committed GPUs and an overflow/ondemand price for spikes. also clarity on prewarm/keepalive costs.
maria_sales: we asked for their p50/p95 — they confirmed p50 250ms, p95 1.2s. also they want canary rollouts and traffic isolation per workspace.
ethan_sre: Ok. Given p95 1.2s and 1.5k tokens, continuous batching to maximize throughput will push p95 above SLO. I'd target dedicated fleet sizing assuming minimal batching (batch size ~1-4). So estimate per GPU 40 qps for worst-case SLO. For 200 qps steady -> 5 GPUs reserved. For 400 qps spike -> 10 GPUs total, so reserve 6 and allow burst to 10 via autoscale credits?
liyah_se: note: model variants — if they accept a 4-bit quantized variant we can double qps per GPU (approx) at modest quality delta. offer a quantized variant as fallback for spikes. that gives economic benefit.
noah_sales_engineering: Can we frame 6 reserved GPUs commit with burst-to-10 for pricing? If reserved monthly cost X, burst at Y higher per-GPU rate. Also include prewarm cost per AZ for canary.
ethan_sre: Yes. Recommend: commit to 6 reserved GPUs (predictable qps 240 headroom), configure autoscale policy with burst pool up to +4 GPUs billed at ondemand rate. Add a fallback model route that uses 4-bit quantized variant during overload windows. Prewarm: 1 GPU warm per AZ during business hours (cost small) to meet cold-start SLOs.
maria_sales: client security Q: will reserved pools be in isolated tenant VPC? they asked about audit logs and KMS.
liyah_se: for Dedicated we can do tenant VPC + customer KMS and forward audit logs to their SIEM. note: enabling KMS + VPC adds ~2 weeks to setup. mention in SOW timeline.
noah_sales_engineering: I'll draft pricing line items: 6x reserved GPUs (monthly), burst credits (pay-as-you-go), prewarm AZ standby (optional line), quantized model license (opt-in discount).
ethan_sre: operational runbook items: autoscale policies: scale-up threshold 85% GPU util OR queue latency > 300ms sustained 20s; scale-down after 5m idle. Configure model fallback logic: traffic routed to quantized variant when queue_length > 50 or p95 latency > 900ms.
maria_sales: client also asked about failure modes — what happens if burst capacity unavailable in region?
ethan_sre: fallback: cross-AZ routing to secondary region (if permitted), otherwise degrade to local quantized variant and return 503-only-if-critical with explanatory header. We'll document RTO and escalation path in runbook.
noah_sales_engineering: good. I'll ask pricing ops to produce numbers and include an SLA appendix. maria — want to hop on 30m call with ACME tomorrow 10am PT?
maria_sales: yes please. I'll send calendar invite and attach preliminary sizing notes. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: [deployment] autoscale-policy update applied to test-cluster (policy-id: as-2234).
liyah_se: one final note — security questionnaire: add note that burst capacity uses same tenant isolation and data plane never leaves customer VPC when Private deployment chosen. we'll include a short paragraph in the security answers.
maria_sales: perfect, thanks everyone. I'll put the 6-reserve / burst-to-10 proposal in the deck and surface the quantized fallback as cost-saving option.
